- If sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) in recent days, reduce forecast slope or shift downward to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, check for overshoot after a spike — cap growth rate or introduce early mean reversion.  
- When true outcome shows sharp drop after a peak, model often overcorrects — adjust forecast to allow for gradual decline rather than abrupt reset.  
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.23) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, consider slight upward bias correction to align with sentiment momentum.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral — reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.  
- If true outcome deviates significantly from forecast in first 5–7 days, apply “lag correction” — adjust forecast to reflect recent history’s mean rather than extrapolation.  
- When sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model often fails to adjust — introduce a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment drops below 0.0.
